messages.subject: lavpredict
parts:
Hello to all,

I have developed a model with 10 endogenous and 10 exogenous variables. I want to predict the endogenous variables from the endogenous one. Is it possible to use lavPredict function like this?

result <- lavPredict(object = fit3,type = "ov", newdata = pred.df, method = "regression",label = T)

If I provide a data frame with NA in endogenous observed variables, I get this error message:

Error in lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan ERROR: some variables have no values (only missings) or no variance


I think an alternative solution could be to solve this

n = solve(I-B))%*%((A%*%p)+k

where B is the matrix of coefficient latent endogenous variables, I is its identity matrix, A matrx of coeff. of exogenous variables, k a matrix of intercepts, p are predictors (exogenous obs. variables)

Does lavaan provide any other solution?

Thanks in advance.
Marcos

On 07/13/2015 02:42 PM, Marcos Angelini wrote:
> Hello to all,
>
> I have developed a model with 10 endogenous and 10 exogenous variables.
> I want to predict the endogenous variables from the endogenous one. Is
> it possible to use lavPredict function like this?
>
> result <- lavPredict(object = fit3,type = "ov", newdata = pred.df,
> method = "regression",label = T)

> If I provide a data frame with NA in endogenous observed variables, I
> get this error message:
>
> Error in lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label =
> group.label, :
> lavaan ERROR: some variables have no values (only missings) or no
> variance

Hm. It works for me. For example:

library(lavaan)
fit <- sem('y2 + y3 + y4 ~ x1 + x2 + x3', data = PoliticalDemocracy)
# create some silly new data
newdata <- as.data.frame(rbind(rnorm(6), rnorm(6), rnorm(6)))
names(newdata) <- lavNames(fit)
lavPredict(fit, type="ov", newdata = newdata, label = TRUE, method =
"regression")

# y2 y3 y4 x1 x2 x3
# [1,] 3.737 2.244 -2.857 0.969 2.737 -0.287
# [2,] 1.947 -0.622 -4.933 0.136 0.119 0.990
# [3,] 0.945 -0.194 -3.741 1.016 -0.893 1.313

# adding some missing values will lead to listwise deletion:
newdata[1,1] <- NA
newdata[2,2] <- NA

lavPredict(fit, type="ov", newdata = newdata, label = TRUE, method =
"regression")

# y2 y3 y4 x1 x2 x3
# [1,] 0.945 -0.194 -3.741 1.016 -0.893 1.313

So you will have to send us a reproducible script to figure out what is
going wrong.

Yves.

OK, I see the original poster has left the building some year ago, but I like to follow up:
I get the same erro when using lavPredict (some variables have no values (only missings) or no variance)
I am a bit confused by this, since it suggests I am getting something completely wrong.

I assumed that with lavPredict, lavaan "simply" fills in the (new) x's in the factor model to calculate y (the factor score). I do not see why it matters if there is no variability in one of the variables. One should also be able to calculate the score of one single person, right?
